Title: ClinicalAgents: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Clinical Decision Making with Dual-Memory
Summary: Proposes ClinicalAgents, a multi-agent clinical decision-making framework in which an Orchestrator uses Monte Carlo Tree Search to generate, test, and backtrack on diagnostic hypotheses, supported by a dual-memory design pairing a mutable working memory of patient state with an experience memory of guidelines and past cases. The authors report state-of-the-art diagnostic accuracy and improved explainability relative to single-agent and other multi-agent baselines.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (Orchestrator with Monte Carlo Tree Search, dual working/experience memory)
Outcome: diagnostic accuracy and explainability vs. single- and multi-agent baselines

Title: MIRA: Medical Image Reflection for Agentic Diagnosis
Summary: Introduces MIRA, an agentic framework for medical image diagnosis that decides when to invoke image tools (zoom, grounding, measurement) or web search and reflects on whether retrieved evidence supports its working hypothesis, trained via a two-stage Monte Carlo Tree Search data engine plus reinforcement learning. Across nine medical visual reasoning benchmarks, MIRA improved its Qwen3-VL-8B backbone by 7.44 points (to an average score of 64.73), raised useful tool-use judgments from 56.2% to 73.8%, and cut harmful tool-use judgments from 8.9% to 1.6%.
AI Technique: LLM agent (tool-augmented, RL + Monte Carlo Tree Search training, Qwen3-VL-8B backbone)
Outcome: medical visual reasoning benchmark accuracy and tool-use judgment quality

Title: An autonomous agentic workflow for clinical detection of cognitive concerns using large language models
Summary: Developed a fully autonomous agentic workflow of five specialized LLM agents that iteratively critique and refine each other's output to screen clinical notes for cognitive concerns, compared against an expert-driven, human-prompted workflow using three LLMs. The autonomous workflow performed comparably to the expert-driven one on validation data (F1 0.74 vs. 0.81) and better on refinement data (0.93 vs. 0.87), with real-world deployment reportedly reaching 98% specificity without further human prompting.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (five specialized self-critiquing/refining agents; Pythia prompt-optimization tool)
Outcome: F1 score and specificity for detecting cognitive concerns in clinical notes

Title: Accelerating Clinical Evidence Synthesis with Large Language Models
Summary: Presents TrialMind, a multi-agent LLM pipeline that generates systematic-review search queries, screens citations, and extracts data from publications while breaking the work into established systematic-review subtasks for expert oversight. In human-AI collaboration, TrialMind yielded a 71.4% recall lift and 44.2% time savings in study screening, and a 23.5% accuracy lift and 63.4% time savings in data extraction, compared with fully manual review.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (TrialMind: query generation, screening, and extraction agents)
Outcome: literature search recall, screening accuracy, and data-extraction accuracy/time savings for systematic reviews

Title: Systematic Literature Reviews With Two Multi-Agentic Systems And Human-In-The-Loop
Summary: Compares a single-agent long-context pipeline (built on Claude Opus 4.7) against two multi-agent system designs for automating systematic literature reviews of randomized controlled trials, with a human-in-the-loop step. The work addresses inconsistent study selection and missed-study bias common in manual screening, evaluating how multi-agent orchestration affects the reliability of study selection and data extraction for meta-analysis.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (vs. single-agent long-context baseline, Claude Opus 4.7)
Outcome: automated systematic review/RCT meta-analysis screening and extraction quality with human-in-the-loop

Title: A Multi-Agent Framework for Medical AI: Leveraging Fine-Tuned GPT, LLaMA, and DeepSeek R1 for Evidence-Based and Bias-Aware Clinical Query Processing
Summary: Proposes a multi-agent medical AI pipeline combining a fine-tuned LLaMA reasoning agent, a PubMed-querying evidence-retrieval agent, and a DeepSeek R1 refinement agent, with built-in uncertainty scoring, bias detection, and an optional human-validation step for clinical query processing. The system reached 87% accuracy with roughly 0.80 relevance and 36.5-second average end-to-end latency, and DeepSeek R1 scored highest on generation metrics, clearly outperforming the biomedical baseline BioGPT in zero-shot evaluation.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (fine-tuned LLaMA reasoning agent, PubMed retrieval agent, DeepSeek R1 refinement agent)
Outcome: clinical query answer accuracy, relevance, and generation quality vs. BioGPT baseline

Title: Large Language Model Agent for Modular Task Execution in Drug Discovery
Journal/Source: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
Summary: Introduces AgentD, a modular LLM agent for early-stage computational drug discovery that performs biomedical data retrieval, literature-grounded question answering via retrieval-augmented generation, molecular generation, multiproperty prediction, property-aware refinement, and 3D protein-ligand structure generation. In a BCL-2 case study, the agent answered mechanistic questions more accurately than standard LLMs and iteratively improved candidate molecules, raising the number passing a drug-likeness (QED > 0.6) threshold from 34 to 55 over two refinement rounds.
AI Technique: LLM agent (AgentD: modular tool-using agent for retrieval, RAG QA, molecular generation, property prediction/refinement, structure generation)
Outcome: task success across modular drug-discovery subtasks (literature QA, molecule generation/property optimization, structure generation)

Title: Artificial intelligence agents in healthcare research: A scoping review
Summary: Scoping review mapping the literature on AI agents in healthcare research, screening over 1,000 records and retaining a core set of recent studies, most from 2025. Found that evaluation has predominantly occurred in simulated or laboratory settings with few clinical pilots or real-world deployments, and that clinical outcomes and safety endpoints are rarely addressed, framing AI-agent research as outpacing translational and governance work.
AI Technique: LLM agent / multi-agent systems (various, scoping review)
Outcome: mapping of evaluation settings, clinical outcomes, and safety reporting across AI-agent healthcare-research studies

Title: Exploring Agentic AI in Healthcare: A Study on Its Working Mechanism
Summary: Conceptual and analytical study examining agentic AI design in healthcare, covering agent decision-making, task allocation, and coordination, with a focus on how 6G networking could support real-time multi-agent orchestration. Illustrates feasibility through a qualitative case study on remote robotic surgery and conducts a SWOT analysis identifying scalability and efficiency gains alongside challenges in ethical governance, system robustness, and security.
AI Technique: Agentic AI (conceptual framework; 6G-enabled multi-agent coordination)
Outcome: conceptual SWOT assessment and case-study feasibility of agentic AI for coordinated healthcare decision-making (illustrated via remote robotic surgery)

Title: Biomedical systems biology workflow orchestration and execution with PoSyMed
Summary: Researchers introduce PoSyMed, a systems-biology agentic workflow system that uses a planning agent to decompose natural-language research requests into subtasks and route them to specialized downstream agents, while maintaining a traceable shared state across the workflow. The system targets reproducible orchestration and execution of multi-step systems-biology analyses without requiring users to write code.
AI Technique: LLM agent (planning agent + specialized agents)
Outcome: systems-biology workflow orchestration/execution reliability

Title: Empowering AI data scientists using a multi-agent LLM framework with self-evolving capabilities for autonomous, tool-aware biomedical data analyses (BioMedAgent)
Summary: A team led by the Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, built a self-evolving multi-agent LLM framework (Planner, Programmer, and Executor agents) that learns to chain diverse bioinformatics tools into executable workflows from natural-language requests. On the new BioMed-AQA benchmark of 327 tasks spanning cross-omics analysis, ML modeling, and pathology image segmentation, the system reached a 77% success rate and generalized robustly to the external BixBench dataset.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (self-evolving Planner/Programmer/Executor agents)
Outcome: automated bioinformatics task success rate

Title: Towards autonomous medical artificial intelligence agents (MIRA)
Summary: Researchers led by Jakob Kather present MIRA (Medical Intelligence for Reasoning and Action), an autonomous agent that operates inside a sandboxed, FHIR-standard EHR environment, ordering labs/imaging/microbiology tests, generating differential diagnoses, and drafting treatment plans. On a head-to-head benchmark subset of 311 real emergency-department cases from MIMIC-IV, MIRA scored 87.8% against 78.1% for a panel of experienced specialists, though the authors caution that results come from simulated, retrospective evaluation and may be inflated by training-data overlap with MIMIC-IV.
AI Technique: LLM agent (MIRA, FHIR-integrated autonomous agent)
Outcome: diagnostic accuracy and treatment planning vs. physicians (simulated ED cases)

Title: The Virtual Biotech: A Multi-Agent AI Framework for Therapeutic Discovery and Development
Summary: Stanford researchers (Zhang, Eckmann, Miao, Mahon, Zou) built the Virtual Biotech, a multi-agent AI framework of roughly 37,000 specialized agents coordinated by a Chief Scientific Officer agent with access to over 100 tools, mirroring the structure of a human therapeutic-discovery organization. The system analyzed 55,984 clinical trials to identify genomic features of drug targets associated with trial success, and used this analysis to propose B7-H3 (CD276) as a lung-cancer drug target via an antibody-drug conjugate strategy, which remains a computational hypothesis requiring experimental validation.
Disease: Lung cancer (case study); N/A (broader trial-success analysis)
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (~37,000 specialized agents)
Outcome: clinical trial success prediction / drug target discovery

Title: Enhancing systematic literature reviews with generative artificial intelligence: development, applications, and performance evaluation
Journal/Source: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association (JAMIA)
Summary: Researchers built a five-module LLM-assisted systematic review system with a human-in-the-loop design, where human-LLM disagreements feed back into refining PICO screening criteria. Evaluated on reviews of relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma and advanced melanoma, the abstract-screening module reached 90% sensitivity, an F1 score of 82, 89% accuracy, and a Cohen's kappa of 0.71 against human reviewers.
AI Technique: LLM (GPT-4-based, five-module human-in-the-loop system)
Outcome: automated literature screening sensitivity/F1/accuracy vs. human reviewers

Title: Artificial intelligence agents in healthcare research: A scoping review
Summary: A scoping review screened 1,070 records down to 43 studies on AI agents used in healthcare, categorizing systems into 8 conversational agents, 17 workflow/automation assistants, and 18 multimodal decision-support agents. The review found that most evaluations were simulated or lab-based, with few real clinical pilots and inconsistent reporting of safety or outcome endpoints.
AI Technique: Agentic AI (review covering LLM agents, workflow automation agents, multimodal decision agents)
Outcome: classification of agent types and evaluation maturity across the agentic-AI-in-healthcare literature

Title: MedCollab: IBIS-Guided Multi-Agent Collaboration with Hierarchical Disease Relation Chains for Clinical Diagnosis
Summary: Researchers proposed MedCollab, a multi-agent framework that emulates hospital hierarchical consultation workflows for full-cycle clinical diagnosis, dynamically recruiting specialist agents and using structured IBIS (Issue-Based Information System) argumentation organized along a hierarchical disease causal chain to link evidence to diagnostic hypotheses. The approach is designed to reduce diagnostic hallucination and improve interpretability compared with single-LLM diagnosis, though independent benchmark numbers were not available.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (dynamic specialist-agent recruitment, IBIS structured argumentation)
Outcome: diagnostic accuracy and interpretability vs. single-LLM diagnosis

Title: AgentSLR: Automating Systematic Literature Reviews in Epidemiology with Agentic AI
Summary: Researchers built AgentSLR, an agentic LLM pipeline for automating epidemiological systematic literature reviews, and validated it on reviews covering nine priority pathogens. The system reportedly performed comparably to human researchers while cutting review time from approximately 7 weeks to about 20 hours.
AI Technique: LLM agent pipeline (literature screening and synthesis)
Outcome: systematic review time reduction and accuracy vs. human researchers

Title: Automating Literature Screening with Multi-Agent Consensus Seeking: A Preliminary Study
Summary: Researchers tested a two-agent LLM screening system with a negotiation/consensus step for systematic-review literature screening. Across five reviews totaling 2,107 articles, the consensus-seeking system outperformed single-agent baselines on accuracy, recall, and F2 score, and correctly excluded 81% of irrelevant records from human review.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (negotiation-based consensus seeking between two agents)
Outcome: automated literature screening accuracy/recall/F2 score (81% correct exclusion of irrelevant records)

Title: Enhancing Evidence Synthesis Efficiency: Leveraging Large Language Models and Agentic Workflows for Optimized Literature Screening
Summary: Researchers built an agentic literature-screening pipeline (GREP-Agent) combining four LLMs with human-in-the-loop feedback, tested on 2,000 citations from a measles-related systematic review. The study reports accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 performance for automated screening, though exact figures were not confirmed in available sources.
AI Technique: Multi-LLM agentic pipeline with human-in-the-loop feedback
Outcome: automated literature screening accuracy/precision/recall/F1

Title: otto-SR: an end-to-end agentic workflow for systematic review automation
Summary: Researchers describe otto-SR, an end-to-end agentic LLM workflow designed to automate the full systematic review pipeline rather than just abstract screening, including reproducing and updating analyses from a set of existing Cochrane systematic reviews.
AI Technique: LLM agent (end-to-end agentic workflow for systematic review automation)
Outcome: reproduction/update accuracy of Cochrane review conclusions

Title: Agentic AI in Healthcare & Medicine: A Seven-Dimensional Taxonomy for Empirical Evaluation of LLM-based Agents
Summary: Researchers systematically reviewed 49 research papers on LLM-based agents deployed in healthcare and medicine, proposing a seven-dimensional taxonomy for evaluating agentic systems empirically. The review found substantial implementation gaps across the surveyed literature, with the authors reporting that roughly 59% of taxonomy dimensions were not actually implemented or evaluated in the papers studied.
AI Technique: LLM agent (systematic review and taxonomy of 49 papers)
Outcome: evaluation-gap analysis across healthcare agentic AI literature

Title: Beyond SMILES: Evaluating Agentic Systems for Drug Discovery
Summary: Researchers evaluated six agentic AI frameworks for drug discovery across 15 task classes spanning peptide therapeutics, in vivo pharmacology, and resource-constrained settings, identifying candidate systems through a literature search of arXiv, PubMed, and Google Scholar. The study found that current agentic systems perform well on computational workflows like SMILES-based small-molecule representation, database queries, and literature mining, but show a substantial "Agent Reality Gap" when applied to multi-objective, real-world drug discovery tasks involving messy multi-modal data from animal studies and wet-lab iteration.
AI Technique: LLM agent (evaluation of 6 agentic drug-discovery frameworks across 15 task classes)
Outcome: generalization/task-success gap of agentic drug-discovery systems beyond small-molecule workflows

Title: Mozi: Governed Autonomy for Drug Discovery LLM Agents
Summary: Researchers built Mozi, a two-layer agentic framework for drug discovery with a governance "Control Plane" that enforces role-based tool isolation and human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and a "Workflow Plane" that models drug-discovery stages (target identification through lead optimization) as stateful, composable skill graphs. Evaluated on PharmaBench, a curated benchmark for biomedical agents, Mozi reportedly achieved superior task-orchestration accuracy over existing baseline agentic systems, with end-to-end case studies reported by the authors.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (supervisor-worker governance layer plus skill-graph workflow layer)
Outcome: orchestration accuracy on PharmaBench drug-discovery benchmark

Title: Large Language Model Agent for Modular Task Execution in Drug Discovery (AgentD)
Journal/Source: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
Summary: Carnegie Mellon researchers developed AgentD, an LLM-powered agent (built primarily on GPT-4o) that automates six drug-discovery pipeline tasks, including literature and database retrieval via UniProt, ChEMBL, and Semantic Scholar APIs, and property prediction using tools like Deep-PK for ADMET and BAPULM for binding affinity. The modular design allows new tools and models to be added as they become available, positioning AgentD as a step toward general-purpose, AI-driven scientific agents for therapeutic discovery.
AI Technique: LLM agent (GPT-4o-based, modular tool-use architecture)
Outcome: automation of drug-discovery pipeline tasks (data retrieval, property prediction)

Title: The Path to Self-Evolving Clinical Systems: Scaling Medical Agents from Assistance to Autonomy
Summary: This survey of more than 300 references models medical AI agents as sequential decision-making systems under partial observability and proposes a three-level autonomy taxonomy spanning assisted, cooperative, and fully autonomous operation. The authors identify integrating agents with clinical tools, data, and "clinical gyms" (PACS, EHR, FHIR environments) as the most actionable yet underexplored direction, and frame self-evolving clinical agents as an aspirational research frontier rather than a solved capability.
AI Technique: LLM agent (survey/taxonomy of medical agent autonomy levels)
Outcome: autonomy-level taxonomy and roadmap for self-evolving clinical agent systems

Title: Large Language Model (LLM)-Based Agentic Artificial Intelligence Tool Streamlines Research Processes in Biomarker Studies: A Proof of Concept
Summary: Researchers built an LLM-based agentic AI tool using retrieval-augmented generation to perform full-text screening for a systematic review of circulating biomarkers in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, applying predefined criteria across thousands of publications. Presented as a proof of concept, the work demonstrates agentic screening as a way to accelerate full-text review stages of cardiovascular systematic reviews.
Disease: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
AI Technique: LLM agent (retrieval-augmented generation for full-text screening)
Outcome: automated full-text screening performance and time savings in a biomarker systematic review

Title: Multi-Agent AI Systems for Biological and Clinical Data Analysis
Summary: A literature review across PubMed, arXiv, ACM, and IEEE Xplore examined multi-agent AI frameworks applied to biological and clinical data analysis, reporting that multi-agent systems reached 87.3% accuracy in clinical trial matching tasks and improved clinician screening efficiency in the studies reviewed. The authors found inter-agent checking reduced errors and improved reasoning transparency, while calling for standardized communication protocols and safety guardrails before wider clinical adoption.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (review of multiple frameworks)
Outcome: clinical trial matching accuracy (87.3%) and screening efficiency across reviewed multi-agent systems

Title: Governing Agentic AI in Healthcare: A Systematic Review of Autonomous Decision-Making, Clinical Safety, and Public Accountability
Summary: A PRISMA-guided systematic review identified 52 studies (34 peer-reviewed, 18 preprints; 32 from 2026) describing autonomous clinical AI agent systems, including patient-facing diagnostic agents, multi-agent transplant-listing committees, and emergency-department pathway engines, each required to demonstrate at least three of four agentic capabilities under a SPIDER framework. The review found the evidence base describes these systems in architectural and safety detail but offers limited empirical documentation of procurement standards, liability allocation, workforce impact, and patient recourse mechanisms.
AI Technique: LLM agent (systematic review of autonomous clinical agent systems)
Outcome: governance/accountability gap analysis across autonomous clinical AI agent literature

Title: AI with Agency: A Vision for Adaptive, Efficient, and Ethical Healthcare
Summary: A perspective proposing an agentic AI framework for healthcare spanning administrative burden reduction, clinical decision-making, and hospital operations such as dynamic staffing, supply, and patient-flow adjustment. The paper is conceptual, outlining a vision rather than reporting empirical deployment results.
AI Technique: LLM agent (conceptual framework)
Outcome: proposed framework for agentic AI across administrative, clinical, and operational healthcare tasks

Title: AI Agents in Drug Discovery
Summary: A review surveying agentic AI architectures in drug discovery, from single-loop ReAct and Reflection patterns to multi-agent Supervisor and Swarm systems, applied to literature synthesis, toxicity prediction, protocol generation, synthesis planning, and drug repurposing. The authors report early implementations compress workflows that once took months into hours, while flagging data heterogeneity, reliability, and benchmarking as open challenges.
AI Technique: LLM agent (review of ReAct, Reflection, Supervisor, Swarm architectures)
Outcome: workflow compression and automation across drug discovery stages

Title: MedAgentBoard: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Collaboration with Conventional Methods for Diverse Medical Tasks
Summary: Introduces a benchmark comparing multi-agent LLM collaboration against single LLMs and conventional methods across four task areas: medical question answering, lay summary generation, structured EHR predictive modeling, and clinical workflow automation. Multi-agent collaboration improved task completeness for workflow automation but did not consistently outperform specialized conventional methods on medical VQA or EHR-based prediction.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (benchmark across 4 task types)
Outcome: comparative task performance of multi-agent vs. single-LLM vs. conventional methods across medical tasks

Title: Orchestrated Multi-Agents Sustain Accuracy Under Clinical-Scale Workloads Compared to a Single Agent
Summary: Mount Sinai researchers compared a single LLM agent handling all tasks against a lightweight multi-agent orchestrator assigning tasks to dedicated workers, across batch sizes of 5-80 simulated clinical tasks. Multi-agent accuracy stayed high (90.6% to 65.3%) while single-agent accuracy collapsed (73.1% to 16.6%), with the multi-agent design also using up to 65 times fewer tokens.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (GPT-4.1 mini orchestrator-worker architecture)
Outcome: task accuracy and token efficiency under scaling clinical workloads

Title: From Siloed Algorithms to Compliance-First Agentic Platforms: A Multi-Layered Architecture for Hospital AI Systems
Journal/Source: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
Summary: Proposes a multi-layered, compliance-first agentic AI architecture for hospital information systems, centralizing policy-as-code for HIPAA, GDPR, the EU AI Act and other regulations alongside a privacy-preserving data layer and multi-agent orchestration across clinical, operational, and financial workflows. Demonstrated on a synthetic hospital dataset for triage risk prediction, workflow optimization, and compliance logging as a prototype rather than a clinically deployed system.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (compliance-first orchestration architecture)
Outcome: architecture proposal for regulatory-compliant agentic hospital AI, demonstrated on synthetic data

Title: From Intention To Implementation: Automating Biomedical Research via LLMs
Summary: Introduces BioResearcher, a multi-agent LLM system spanning search, literature processing, experimental design, and programming modules to automate the dry-lab biomedical research pipeline from objective to executable protocol. BioResearcher achieved a 63.07% average execution success rate across eight novel research objectives and outperformed typical agent systems by 22.0% on protocol quality metrics.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (Search, Literature Processing, Experimental Design, Programming modules)
Outcome: automated research protocol execution success rate (63.07%)

Title: Biomni: A General-Purpose Biomedical AI Agent
Summary: Stanford researchers introduced Biomni, a biomedical AI agent combining an action environment (Biomni-E1, with 150 tools, 105 software packages and 59 databases) with an LLM-driven planning agent (Biomni-A1) that builds workflows without fixed templates. The system reported strong performance across tasks including causal gene prioritization, drug repurposing, rare disease diagnosis, microbiome analysis, and molecular cloning without task-specific prompt tuning.
AI Technique: LLM agent (retrieval-based planning + code execution, Biomni-E1/A1)
Outcome: task success across diverse biomedical research tasks (gene prioritization, drug repurposing, rare disease diagnosis, etc.)

Title: Process-Supervised Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Reliable Clinical Reasoning
Summary: University of Edinburgh researchers built a hierarchical multi-agent system with a supervisor agent coordinating specialized sub-agents for gene-disease validity curation on the ClinGen dataset, trained with combined outcome- and process-based reinforcement learning rewards. Adding process supervision raised outcome accuracy to 0.750 (from 0.732 with outcome-only rewards) while improving process-fidelity F1 from 0.392 to 0.520, with better robustness on unseen data than a single-agent baseline.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (hierarchical supervisor + sub-agents, GRPO reinforcement learning, Qwen3-4B)
Outcome: gene-disease validity curation accuracy (outcome accuracy 0.750, process F1 0.520)

Title: The Doctor Will (Still) See You Now: On the Structural Limits of Agentic AI in Healthcare
Summary: Qualitative study based on interviews with 20 stakeholders, including developers and physicians, examining the gap between agentic AI marketed as autonomous and its actual near-total human oversight in practice due to safety, regulatory, and liability constraints. Argues that current medical AI evaluation frameworks, which emphasize technical performance metrics, fail to capture the oversight and accountability demands agentic systems create.
AI Technique: N/A (qualitative stakeholder study of agentic AI deployment)
Outcome: assessment of human oversight requirements and evaluation gaps in agentic healthcare AI

Title: Agentic AI, Medical Morality, and the Transformation of the Patient-Physician Relationship
Summary: Ethics paper applying a techno-moral change framework (decision, relation, and perception domains) to examine how goal-directed, task-coordinating agentic AI systems may reshape the patient-physician relationship and core medical-ethical concepts. Argues the resulting shifts are not fully predictable but warrant ethical foresight built into agentic AI design before widespread clinical deployment.
AI Technique: N/A (ethical/conceptual analysis of agentic AI)
Outcome: ethical analysis of agentic AI's impact on the patient-physician relationship

Title: Deep Research Agents: Major Breakthrough or Incremental Progress for Medical AI?
Summary: JMIR viewpoint arguing that LLM-based "deep research agents," which automate literature retrieval and synthesis for medical research, represent an incremental evolution rather than a paradigm shift for medical AI. Notes that supporting evidence remains mostly proof-of-concept with little real-world clinical deployment, and flags opaque retrieval and evidence-ranking mechanisms as reproducibility and bias concerns, recommending the tools be treated as assistive research aids rather than pseudoexperts.
AI Technique: LLM agent (deep research / literature retrieval and synthesis agents)
Outcome: assessment of deep research agent reliability and clinical research utility

Title: AI Agents in Clinical Medicine: A Systematic Review
Summary: Systematic review searching PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus (October 2022-August 2025) for studies of AI agent systems in clinical medicine, identifying 20 qualifying studies spanning single-agent tool-calling, multi-agent without tools, and hybrid multi-agent-plus-tool architectures. Found that all agent systems outperformed their baseline LLMs, with the largest accuracy gains when agent-framework complexity matched task complexity, and multi-agent systems (up to five agents) performing best on highly complex tasks.
AI Technique: LLM agent (systematic review of single- and multi-agent architectures)
Outcome: comparative accuracy of AI agent systems vs. baseline LLMs on clinical tasks

Title: OpenScientist: Evaluating an Open Agentic AI Co-Scientist to Accelerate Biomedical Discovery
Summary: Introduces OpenScientist, an open-source agentic AI co-scientist that semi-autonomously investigates scientist-defined research queries, evaluated across four clinical case studies. Reported completing analyses in minutes that would otherwise take weeks to months of human effort, demonstrating the feasibility of open, auditable agentic support for real-world clinical research.
AI Technique: LLM agent (open-source agentic co-scientist)
Outcome: biomedical research task completion time and feasibility vs. manual analysis

Title: BioVerge: A Comprehensive Benchmark and Study of Self-Evaluating Agents for Biomedical Hypothesis Generation
Summary: Introduces BioVerge, a benchmark built from historical biomedical hypotheses and PubMed literature, and BioVerge Agent, a ReAct-based agent with separate hypothesis-generation and self-evaluation modules tested in single- and double-agent configurations. Found that self-evaluation improves hypothesis novelty and relevance and that combining structured and textual data sources helps, though evaluation was limited to diabetes research.
AI Technique: LLM agent (ReAct, self-evaluating generation/evaluation modules)
Outcome: novelty and relevance of generated biomedical research hypotheses

Title: AUTOCT: Automating Interpretable Clinical Trial Prediction With LLM Agents
Summary: Proposes AUTOCT, a framework pairing LLM-agent reasoning with interpretable classical machine learning, where the agent autonomously generates, scores, and refines tabular features from public information and uses Monte Carlo Tree Search for self-refinement. On clinical trial prediction tasks from TrialBench (adverse events, trial failure, mortality, patient dropout, approval), the system matched or exceeded state-of-the-art methods using only a limited number of refinement iterations.
AI Technique: LLM agent (feature-engineering agent with Monte Carlo Tree Search, paired with classical ML)
Outcome: clinical trial outcome prediction (adverse events, failure, mortality, dropout, approval) vs. state-of-the-art

Title: H-AdminSim: A Multi-Agent Simulator for Realistic Hospital Administrative Workflows With FHIR Integration
Journal/Source: PMLR (Conference on Health, Inference, and Learning 2026)
Summary: Introduces H-AdminSim, a multi-agent simulation framework that generates realistic dialogue-based hospital outpatient administrative workflows (e.g., intake, appointment scheduling) grounded in FHIR resources, filling a gap left by prior work focused on patient-physician interaction rather than administrative tasks. Evaluates LLMs on the simulated workflows using detailed task rubrics, enabling systematic comparison across hospital scales.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (FHIR-grounded simulation)
Outcome: feasibility and rubric-based evaluation of LLM-driven hospital administrative workflow automation

Title: When OpenClaw Meets Hospital: Toward an Agentic Operating System for Dynamic Clinical Workflows
Summary: Argues that general-purpose agent orchestration frameworks like OpenClaw lack the execution isolation, audit trails, and clinically structured memory needed for hospitals, and proposes an 'Agentic Operating System' with a restricted execution environment, page-indexed hierarchical memory, document-mediated multi-agent coordination, and a medical skills library. Reports that hierarchical memory navigation is most valuable when queries span multiple care episodes, outlining a practical path toward hospital-scale agentic infrastructure.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (agentic operating system architecture)
Outcome: feasibility of safe, auditable multi-agent coordination for dynamic hospital clinical workflows

Title: AgentRx: A Benchmark Study of LLM Agents for Multimodal Clinical Prediction Tasks
Journal/Source: PMLR (Conference on Health, Inference, and Learning 2026)
Summary: Benchmarks single- and multi-agent LLM frameworks on unimodal and multimodal clinical risk-prediction tasks using MIMIC ICU data spanning EHR time series, medical images, radiology reports, and clinical notes. Found single-agent frameworks outperformed naive multi-agent systems on multimodal data handling and calibration, while a supervised baseline model still outperformed all LLM agents on multimodal mortality prediction.
AI Technique: LLM agent (single- vs. multi-agent comparison)
Outcome: multimodal clinical risk/mortality prediction accuracy and calibration vs. supervised baselines

Title: AutoSynthesis: An Agentic System for Automated Meta-Analysis
Summary: Introduces AutoSynthesis, a multi-agent pipeline that takes a natural-language research question and automates an entire meta-analysis, including search strategy, random-effects pooling, heterogeneity analysis, publication-bias diagnostics, risk-of-bias assessment, and PRISMA-aligned reporting. In a case study replicating an expert meta-analysis of LLM persuasion, the system recovered 71.4% (85.7% accounting for one inaccessible full text) of benchmark studies with a pooled effect estimate within 0.123 Hedges' g of the human analysis.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (automated meta-analysis pipeline)
Outcome: automated meta-analysis study-recovery rate and pooled effect-size accuracy vs. expert benchmark

Title: Completing A Systematic Review in Hours Instead of Months With Interactive AI Agents
Summary: Presents an interactive multi-agent system (InsightAgent) that lets a single domain expert complete a biomedical systematic review in about 1.5 hours while reaching 79.7% of human-written review quality, evaluated against 15 existing biomedical systematic reviews with 9 domain experts and medical students. Reported a 15.6% quality improvement over the AutoSurvey baseline and a 27.2% quality gain attributable to its visualization and interaction mechanisms, though the system was limited to reading abstracts rather than full texts.
AI Technique: LLM agent (interactive multi-agent system, GPT-4o backbone)
Outcome: systematic review completion time and quality vs. human-written reviews

Title: LatteReview: A Multi-Agent Framework for Systematic Review Automation Using Large Language Models
Summary: Introduces LatteReview, an open-source Python framework in which multiple LLM agents (e.g., junior reviewers plus a senior GPT-4o adjudicator) collaborate to automate title/abstract screening, relevance scoring, and structured data extraction for systematic reviews. Testing across six public systematic review datasets found multi-agent LLM systems can meaningfully automate screening, with performance improving when review criteria and workflow design are well specified.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (junior/senior reviewer agents)
Outcome: title/abstract screening automation accuracy across systematic review datasets

Title: ClinicalReTrial: Clinical Trial Redesign with Self-Evolving Agents
Summary: Introduced a self-evolving multi-agent system that iteratively redesigns failed clinical trial protocols through coordinated failure diagnosis, protocol modification, and candidate evaluation stages, using a LightGBM-based prediction model trained on over 12,000 TrialBench trials as a simulated scoring environment. Tested on 60 failed Phase I-IV trials (enrollment, safety, and efficacy failures), the system improved the majority of redesigned protocols with a mean success-probability gain of roughly 5.7%, at about $0.12 per trial.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (GPT-4o-mini agents with LightGBM evaluator)
Outcome: automated clinical trial protocol redesign success-probability improvement

Title: DiscoVerse: Multi-Agent Pharmaceutical Co-Scientist for Traceable Drug Discovery and Reverse Translation
Summary: Presented DiscoVerse, a modular multi-agent system acting as a pharmaceutical co-scientist, with specialized agents coordinating traceable drug discovery and reverse-translation tasks end to end. The framework emphasizes auditability of each agent's reasoning and contributions across the discovery pipeline.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (pharmaceutical co-scientist)
Outcome: traceable, automated drug discovery and reverse-translation workflow

Title: AgentRx: A Benchmark Study of LLM Agents for Multimodal Clinical Prediction Tasks
Summary: Systematically benchmarked single-agent and multi-agent LLM systems (7-8B parameter models) on unimodal and multimodal clinical prediction tasks using harmonized MIMIC-IV, MIMIC-CXR, and MIMIC-IV-Note data. Found single-agent frameworks outperformed naive multi-agent systems and were better calibrated, though a supervised baseline (MedPatch, AUROC 0.877) still outperformed all LLM agents on multimodal mortality prediction.
AI Technique: LLM agent (single- and multi-agent comparison, 7-8B models)
Outcome: multimodal clinical prediction (e.g., mortality) accuracy and calibration of LLM agents vs. supervised baselines

Title: From Literature to Hypotheses: An AI Co-Scientist System for Biomarker-Guided Drug Combination Hypothesis Generation
Summary: Developed CoDHy, an interactive, human-in-the-loop AI co-scientist system that mines the literature to generate biomarker-guided drug combination hypotheses for cancer research. The system is designed to support researchers in identifying candidate drug combinations tied to specific biomarkers rather than fully automating hypothesis generation.
AI Technique: LLM agent (human-in-the-loop AI co-scientist)
Outcome: biomarker-guided drug combination hypothesis generation

Title: Democratizing Drug Discovery with an Orchestrated, Knowledge-Driven Multi-Agent Team for User-Guided Therapeutic Design
Summary: Introduced OrchestRA, a multi-agent system with specialized Biologist, Chemist, and Pharmacologist agents coordinated by an orchestrator that translates natural-language prompts into executable therapeutic-design workflows. The Biologist Agent mines a large curated biomedical knowledge graph for targets, the Chemist Agent performs structure-based molecule design, and the Pharmacologist Agent evaluates candidates via physiologically based pharmacokinetic simulations, with a feedback loop triggering structural reoptimization based on toxicity/PK results.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (Biologist/Chemist/Pharmacologist agents)
Outcome: automated end-to-end drug target identification, molecule design, and PBPK-based candidate evaluation

Title: H-AdminSim: A Multi-Agent Simulator for Realistic Hospital Administrative Workflows with FHIR Integration
Summary: Built H-AdminSim, a multi-agent LLM simulator of dialogue-based outpatient hospital administrative workflows (first-visit scheduling, rescheduling, cancellations) across primary, secondary, and tertiary hospital settings, using FHIR resources to represent clinical administrative data. Tasks are scored against detailed rubrics, and the authors present it as the first simulator to apply FHIR to hospital administration.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (FHIR-integrated administrative simulation)
Outcome: simulated hospital administrative task completion/accuracy (scheduling, rescheduling, cancellations)

Title: HealthAgentBench: A Unified Benchmark Suite of Realistic Agentic Healthcare Environments for Challenging Frontier AI Agents
Summary: Introduced HealthAgentBench, a benchmark suite of realistic agentic healthcare environments-including a clinical trial matching task in which agents read free-text admission notes and candidate trial criteria to judge eligibility-designed to evaluate frontier AI agents against physician-judged gold standards. The suite spans multiple agentic healthcare tasks beyond trial matching to stress-test tool use and reasoning in realistic clinical settings.
AI Technique: LLM agent (benchmark evaluation of frontier agents)
Outcome: agentic task performance (incl. clinical trial eligibility matching) vs. physician-judged gold standards

Title: Towards AI-Assisted Clinical Trial Matching: Practical Considerations, Multicenter Evaluation, and Real-World Deployment
Summary: Reported a multicenter evaluation and real-world deployment of an AI-assisted clinical trial patient-matching system, with outputs reviewed in routine practice between February and July 2026 across 27 cases and 339 patient-trial pairs. The study addresses practical deployment considerations for automating what is otherwise a largely manual, error-prone trial-matching process.
AI Technique: LLM agent (clinical trial matching, real-world deployment)
Outcome: real-world clinical trial patient-matching accuracy and deployment feasibility

Title: AI-Assisted Workflow Enables Rapid, High-Fidelity Breast Cancer Clinical Trial Eligibility Prescreening
Summary: Developed an AI-assisted prescreening workflow for breast cancer clinical trial eligibility that reported 98.6% patient-level accuracy while cutting manual screening time from about 20 minutes to 43 seconds per case, at roughly $0.96 per patient-trial pair. The system is positioned to substantially reduce the manual burden of trial eligibility prescreening in oncology.
AI Technique: LLM agent (automated eligibility prescreening workflow)
Outcome: clinical trial eligibility prescreening accuracy (98.6%) and screening time/cost reduction

Title: Toward an AI Reasoning-Enabled System for Patient-Clinical Trial Matching
Summary: Proposed a proof-of-concept system using the DeepSeek-R1 reasoning model to extract 14 key clinical data categories from EHRs and assess patient eligibility against trial inclusion/exclusion criteria, producing reasoning, certainty levels, and "Eligible Now"/"Not Eligible" labels. In preliminary assessments, the majority of patient-trial pairs (88%) were classified as "Not Eligible," consistent with known imbalances in real-world trial matching, though the authors note the work lacks independent accuracy validation.
AI Technique: LLM agent (DeepSeek-R1 reasoning model)
Outcome: patient-trial eligibility classification and reasoning (proof-of-concept)

Title: A Multi-Agent Framework for Interpreting Multivariate Physiological Time Series (Vivaldi)
Summary: Gabrielli et al. present Vivaldi, a role-structured multi-agent system mirroring an emergency department team (triage, doctor, consultant, coder, synthesizer agents) that explains multivariate physiological time series. In a pilot with emergency medicine experts, agentic orchestration improved diagnostic precision for thinking models (ESI F1 +3.6) and improved expert-rated justification for non-thinking and medically fine-tuned models, though it sometimes lowered explanation quality for reasoning models.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (role-structured ED-team agents)
Outcome: interpretability and diagnostic precision of physiological time-series explanations

Title: Small Agent Group is the Future of Digital Health
Summary: Meng, Xi et al. propose SAG, a group of small LLM agents that deliberate together on clinical reasoning tasks, with combined parameter count comparable to or smaller than a single large model. The authors report SAG outperforms a single giant LLM on effectiveness, reliability, and deployment cost, both with and without additional optimization such as Group Relative Policy Optimization or retrieval-augmented generation.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (small deliberating agents, GRPO)
Outcome: clinical reasoning performance versus deployment cost

Title: AgentEHR: Advancing Autonomous Clinical Decision-Making via Retrospective Summarization
Summary: Liao et al. introduce AgentEHR, a benchmark testing whether LLM agents can work through raw MIMIC-IV/MIMIC-III EHR databases to make diagnosis and treatment decisions across six clinical tasks, plus RetroSum, a method combining retrospective summarization with an evolving experience memory bank. RetroSum reported performance gains of up to 29.16% over competitive baselines while reducing total interaction errors by up to 92.3%.
AI Technique: LLM agent (retrospective summarization with experience memory)
Outcome: autonomous clinical decision-making accuracy over raw EHR databases

Title: EHRNavigator: A Multi-Agent System for Patient-Level Clinical Question Answering over Heterogeneous Electronic Health Records
Summary: Qian et al. developed EHRNavigator, a multi-agent system with a SQL Writer Agent for structured EHR tables, a note retrieval tool for unstructured text, and an Answer Synthesizer Agent integrating both evidence types to answer patient-level clinical questions. Evaluated on a public benchmark and institutional datasets with clinician-validated chart review, it reached 86% accuracy on real-world cases with clinically acceptable response times.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (SQL agent + retrieval agent + synthesizer agent)
Outcome: accuracy of patient-level clinical question answering over heterogeneous EHR data (86%)

Title: ClinSeekAgent: Automating Multimodal Evidence Seeking for Agentic Clinical Reasoning
Summary: Wu et al. built ClinSeekAgent, an agent that actively seeks its own multimodal evidence (web search, raw EHR retrieval, chest X-ray imaging tools) rather than relying on pre-curated context, alongside ClinSeek-Bench for evaluation. On the multimodal benchmark it improved 5 of 6 evaluated models, with Claude Opus 4.6 improving from 47.5 to 62.6 overall F1, and a distilled open-source model (ClinSeek-35B-A3B) improved 11.9 points over its base model on an external EHR-agent benchmark.
AI Technique: LLM agent (active multimodal evidence-seeking, distilled open-source variant)
Outcome: clinical reasoning accuracy (F1) with actively acquired versus pre-curated multimodal evidence

Title: AgentsEval: Clinically Faithful Evaluation of Medical Imaging Reports via Multi-Agent Reasoning
Summary: Fu et al. propose AgentsEval, a multi-agent stream-reasoning evaluator for medical imaging reports that splits scoring into criteria definition, evidence extraction, alignment, and consistency scoring to mirror radiologist reasoning and produce an inspectable trace. On a perturbation-based benchmark built from five public report datasets (paraphrase, semantic, and factual changes), the authors report it outperforms traditional and single-agent LLM evaluators and remains robust under perturbations.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (stepwise criteria/evidence/alignment scoring)
Outcome: clinical faithfulness and robustness of automated medical imaging report evaluation

Title: Multi-Modal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Radiology Report Generation: Radiologist-Like Workflow with Clinically Verifiable Rewards (MARL-Rad)
Summary: Baba and Kodera present MARL-Rad, which decomposes chest X-ray interpretation into region-specific agents plus a global integrating agent, jointly trained end-to-end via reinforcement learning with clinically verifiable rewards rather than wrapping independently trained models into an agent pipeline. On MIMIC-CXR and IU X-ray, the system reported state-of-the-art clinical efficacy metrics (RadGraph F1, CheXbert F1, GREEN score) and improved laterality consistency, with blinded clinician evaluation rating reports as clinically comparable to ground truth.
AI Technique: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (region-specific + global integrating agents)
Outcome: clinical efficacy and accuracy of automated radiology report generation

Title: MARC v1: An Open-Source Multi-Agent Framework for Clinical AI Reasoning and Coordination
Summary: Shetty, Tripathi and colleagues from UC Davis, Penn, and Drexel built MARC, an open-source framework replacing single-prompt LLM answers with deterministic multi-agent orchestration, using role-specific agents for extraction, reasoning, answer generation, and evaluation that pass context explicitly so failures can be traced to a specific stage. A decomposer module auto-generates task-specific agent prompts from a plain-language task description, removing manual prompt engineering, and the framework supports both API-based and local CPU-compatible deployment configured via YAML.
AI Technique: Multi-agent LLM system (role-specific pipeline with auto-generated prompts)
Outcome: traceability and configurability of multi-agent clinical AI reasoning pipelines
